```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# All figures on these slides are generated here from the course data files
# (../data/*.csv) or from small inline tribbles of published summary values –
# no images of the Nature papers' figures are used (copyright + everything must
# stay editable). Palette mirrors style/cgm-slides.scss.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(readr)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(purrr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(dagitty)
  library(ggdag)
  library(patchwork)
})

ncl_blue <- "#0e3b6a"
orange   <- "#E69F00"
green    <- "#009E73"
d_red    <- "#a10000"
grey_mid <- "#848c94"

# A light slide-friendly ggplot theme: big type, no chart-junk.
theme_slide <- function(base_size = 17) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey90"),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", colour = ncl_blue),
      axis.title = element_text(colour = ncl_blue),
      legend.position = "none"
    )
}

# The four-cell repeatability matrix (Nosek et al. 2025). Defined once here so
# the full-colour slide and the 'robustness only' emphasis slide draw from a
# single source of truth – no copy-pasted plot code to drift apart. The data x
# analysis matrix is rendered as a tile grid (inline data, not a screenshot) so
# it stays fully editable; the term sits large in each cell with its one-line
# meaning beneath it.
repeatability_cells <- tibble::tribble(
  ~analysis,    ~data,       ~term,             ~def,                                  ~fill,
  "SAME METHODS",      "SAME DATA", "Reproducibility", "Testing the reliability of a prior finding\nwith the same data and same analysis\nstrategy by comparing the outcome of an\ninferential test as reported in a paper\nwith a re-calculation of that inferential\ntest from the original data.", "#0e3b6a",
  "DIFFERENT METHODS", "SAME DATA", "Robustness",  "Testing the reliability of a prior finding\nwith the same data and different analysis\nstrategy by conducting alternative\ntests on the original data.",  "#E69F00",
  "SAME METHODS",      "DIFFERENT DATA",  "Replicability",   "Testing the reliability of a prior finding\nwith new data expected to be theoretically\nequivalent by comparing the outcome of an\ninferential test as reported in a paper\nwith the equivalent inferential test as\ncalculated in the new dataset.",               "#009E73",
  "DIFFERENT METHODS", "DIFFERENT DATA", "Generalisability", "Testing the reliability of a prior finding\nin a new dataset in a way that differs\nfrom the original study but is expected\nto produce similar results.",                 "#834848"
)

# Draw the matrix. `highlight = NULL` keeps all four cells in full colour; pass
# a term (e.g. "Robustness") to dim every OTHER cell to a light-grey box. Text
# stays white throughout, so dimmed cells read as light-grey background + white
# text while the highlighted cell keeps its own colour.
repeatability_matrix <- function(highlight = NULL) {
  grey_box <- "#b6bcc3"   # light grey for de-emphasised cells
  cells <- repeatability_cells |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      data = factor(data, levels = c("SAME DATA", "DIFFERENT DATA")),
      analysis = factor(analysis,
        levels = c("DIFFERENT METHODS", "SAME METHODS")),
      fill = if (is.null(highlight)) fill
             else dplyr::if_else(term == highlight, fill, grey_box)
    )
  ggplot(cells, aes(data, analysis)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = fill), colour = "white", linewidth = 4,
              width = 1, height = 1) +
    geom_text(aes(label = term), colour = "white",
              fontface = "bold", size = 9, nudge_y = 0.25) +
    geom_text(aes(label = def), colour = "white",
              size = 5, nudge_y = -0.1, lineheight = 0.95) +
    scale_fill_identity() +
    scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_void(20) +
    # Row labels flipped to read vertically (bottom-to-top), matching the
    # rotated row-heads on the HTML image-grid version of this matrix.
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
          axis.text = element_text(face = "bold", colour = ncl_blue),
          axis.text.x.top = element_text(size = 17),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 15, angle = 90, hjust = 0.5),
          plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(2, 8, 2, 2))
}

# Read the two data files that the multiverse slides depend on. Relative paths
# resolve from slides/ at render time (verified with quarto render).
# r_ca is the claim-aligned partial r – the day's convention: negative framings
# (mcomm, mlib, mneg) reverse-coded, so 'supports the claim' = negative sign
# for every outcome. All Part 4 curve/placement slides work on this scale;
# the class chart and the lab's percentile cell use the same one.
spec_grid <- readr::read_csv("../data/spec_grid.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(r_ca = ifelse(positive_outcome, r, -r))
analysts5 <- readr::read_csv("../data/analysts5.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# The 29 teams of Silberzahn et al. (2018), published values, read here because
# two slides in different parts draw them: the full forest in Part 1 and the
# one-row reminder strip in Part 2. Codebook: data/silberzahn29_codebook.md.
silberzahn29 <- readr::read_csv("../data/silberzahn29.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(distribution = factor(distribution,
                  levels = c("Linear", "Logistic", "Poisson", "Other")))

# Teams described their own methods and capitalised them 29 different ways;
# the published table title-cases them, and the forest slide follows suit.
tidy_approach <- function(x) {
  stringr::str_replace_all(stringr::str_to_title(x),
                           "\\b(And|A|For|With|Using|The|Of)\\b", tolower)
}

# Shared multiverse base layer, mirroring the build-time chart on the
# Multiverse page (results.qmd) so the room sees one visual grammar in the
# deck and on the page collecting its dots: the full universe of 2,520
# specifications (data/spec_grid_full.csv), each family ranked within itself;
# colour carries the outcome family, the marker the claim-carrying predictor,
# faded points miss 5% significance, and the shaded band above zero runs
# against the claim. Claim alignment matches the page too: negative framings
# reverse-coded, growth predictors sign-flipped on top (their claim-expected
# sign is positive). Built ONCE so the two consecutive multiverse slides
# ("The class multiverse" and "Where your result lands") are the SAME chart
# with an overlay, not two charts: identical dims, axes, theme and legend
# slots, so the reveal animates the analyst tags appearing on one unchanging
# panel. coord_cartesian() pins the y-range so the overlay cannot rescale
# the axis between slides.
spec_full <- readr::read_csv("../data/spec_grid_full.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(r_ca = r * ifelse(positive_outcome, 1, -1) *
                  ifelse(predictor == "growth", -1, 1)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(family, r_ca) |>
  dplyr::mutate(rank = dplyr::row_number(), .by = family)
sc_baseline <- dplyr::filter(spec_full, baseline, family == "gaussian")

spec_base <- function() {
  ggplot(spec_full, aes(rank, r_ca)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = 0, ymax = Inf,
             fill = d_red, alpha = 0.045) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = grey_mid, linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = family, shape = predictor, alpha = sig),
               size = 1.2, stroke = 0.4) +
    geom_point(data = sc_baseline, shape = 2, size = 3.2, stroke = 1.1,
               colour = orange) +
    annotate("text", x = sc_baseline$rank, y = sc_baseline$r_ca - 0.14,
             label = "constrained baseline\nt = −3.804",
             colour = orange, fontface = "bold", size = 4, hjust = 0) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(gaussian = ncl_blue, beta = green),
                        breaks = c("gaussian", "beta"),
                        labels = c("gaussian family", "beta family"),
                        name = NULL,
                        guide = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(
                          shape = 16, size = 2.6, alpha = 1))) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(unemp = 2, growth = 0),
                       breaks = c("unemp", "growth"),
                       labels = c("unemployment", "GDP growth"),
                       name = NULL,
                       guide = guide_legend(order = 2, override.aes = list(
                         colour = "grey30", size = 2.6, stroke = 0.8,
                         alpha = 1))) +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 0.9, `FALSE` = 0.25),
                       breaks = c(TRUE, FALSE),
                       labels = c("p < .05", "n.s."),
                       name = NULL,
                       guide = guide_legend(order = 3, override.aes = list(
                         shape = 16, size = 2.6, colour = grey_mid))) +
    labs(x = "specification (ranked by claim-aligned partial r within family)",
         y = "claim-aligned partial r") +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.75, 0.45)) +
    theme_slide(15) +
    theme(legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_blank())
}

# Fork-importance decomposition over the committed grid
# (data/fork_importance.csv: share of specification variance in partial r per
# menu axis, main-effects eta-squared). Read once; the Part 4 slide charts it.
fork_imp <- readr::read_csv("../data/fork_importance.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Analyst placement inside the 840-spec grid: the share of the grid more
# negative than each analyst's recorded partial r, on the claim-aligned scale
# (the analysts' own values are cosmopolitan-outcome results, so alignment
# leaves them untouched). The person/aggregate split is the published
# classification of the five Multi100 pipelines (KEVF1 and PRL47 fitted
# person-level models; the other three worked on aggregates).
an_level <- tibble::tribble(
  ~analyst_id, ~level,
  "KEVF1", "person-level",
  "PRL47", "person-level",
  "KQXUE", "aggregated",
  "018OL", "aggregated",
  "C6HJR", "aggregated"
)
an_placed <- analysts5 |>
  dplyr::left_join(an_level, by = "analyst_id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_more_negative = purrr::map_dbl(r, \(x) mean(spec_grid$r_ca < x)) * 100) |>
  dplyr::arrange(pct_more_negative)

# Wrong-sign specifications in the cosmopolitan-only universe: the claim
# predicts a negative unemployment coefficient on mcosmo, so a positive
# estimate is a sign flip. Cross-tabbed by estimator and sample on the
# Part 4 patterned-flips slide.
flips_mcosmo <- spec_grid |>
  dplyr::filter(outcome == "mcosmo") |>
  dplyr::mutate(wrong_sign = estimate > 0)
```
